iterations.strategy: Root cause: scan_mi_csr_and_filter (26ms, 38% of total) wastes varlen offset+data reads on year-failing rows because LIKE check runs before the year filter; main_scan touches a 16MB aka_name offsets array per surviving ci row, exceeding LLC. Strategy: Category A+C (plan restructuring + work elimination). (1) Build a compact Y bitset over title.id (production_year > 2000 AND != INT32_MIN, ~316KB → L2). In the CSR scan, look up Y[mv] FIRST (after computing mv from mi_movie_id[r]); skip mi_info_off and mi_info_dat reads for rows whose movie fails the year filter — eliminates ~50% of varlen accesses, saving ~10-12ms. (2) Fuse three name-side filters into a single P_and_an bitset over name.id (gender='f' ∧ name LIKE '%An%' ∧ aka_name nonempty, ~520KB → L2). One bit test per ci row replaces a bit test + a separate 16MB cache-exceeding aka_name offsets random probe — should shave ~2-3ms from main_scan. Expected total: ~52-55ms vs 68ms baseline. No changes to threshold_constant 2000 (year cutoff preserved verbatim).

Iter 1 reduced total 68->66ms but scan_mi_csr_year_first_then_like still dominates at 24ms (36% of total). Diagnosis: after Y bitset prunes ~50% of release_dates rows, the remaining ~4M rows still do random varlen reads into mi_info.off (118MB) and mi_info.dat (626MB) — both vastly exceeding L3 (12MB). Only ~30-40% of these rows actually start with 'Japan:' or 'USA:', so 60-70% of varlen reads are wasted. Strategy: Category E (storage extension). Built column_versions/movie_info.info.prefix_dict — a uint16 dict-encoded column where each mi row's code is the dict id of its letter-only prefix-before-colon (or 0 if no usable prefix). At query time, resolve 'Japan' and 'USA' to codes once, then in the CSR scan check prefix_codes[r] ∈ {japan_code, usa_code} BEFORE reading info.off/info.dat. The codes column is 29MB strided-sequential in CSR order, far cheaper than random probes into 744MB of varlen data. Expected: scan_mi drops from 24ms to ~10-13ms. All other phases (build_Y, build_P, main_scan) unchanged. Year threshold 2000 preserved verbatim.

Iter_2 plan said to use prefix_dict but the generated code (lines 314-355 of iter_2/q19c.cpp) never read codes.bin — it did the same Y→varlen flow as iter_1, so scan_mi stayed at 24ms. Iter_3 strategy: Category A (filter reordering) + Category E (use existing storage extension). Two changes: (1) MANDATORY use of column_versions/movie_info.info.prefix_dict/codes.bin — mmap it as const uint16_t* prefix_codes. (2) Reorder the CSR inner loop so prefix_codes[r] is checked FIRST, BEFORE mi_mid[r]. Rationale: prefix_codes is 16MB strided-sequential (bandwidth-bound, ~2-3ms for 8M reads on 12 threads); mi_mid[r] is 58MB random — but if we filter on code first, ~99% of rows never read mi_mid at all. Y bitset check moves to position 3, only hit by ~80K-160K survivors. Resolve japan_code and usa_code once at startup by linear-scanning the 19351-entry dict (1-based ids per registry). For survivors, the prefix length is known (6 for Japan:, 4 for USA:), so we skip the string prefix re-compare and go directly to memmem('200', tail). Expected: scan_mi 24ms → 8-12ms; total 63ms → ~45-50ms. Year threshold 2000 and the four voice-note strings are preserved verbatim.

Iter_4 takes a DIFFERENT direction from iter_3 (which regressed). Root cause: scan_mi at 24ms (38% of total) is dominated by strided access into mi_movie_id (58MB), mi_info_off (118MB), and mi_info_dat (626MB) while walking the it_rd CSR slice (8M rows). All three are L3-exceeding and accessed in strided/random fashion. Strategy: Category B (algorithm change) + Category E (use storage extension). Abandon the CSR-driven scan entirely. Drive the scan with a SEQUENTIAL pass over the 29.5MB prefix_codes column (storage extension): each thread sweeps a contiguous range of mi rows, doing one uint16 compare per row. The prefix filter rejects ~99.7% of rows (only ~30K-60K of 14.8M mi rows have Japan/USA prefix), and rejected rows incur zero further memory touches. For the tiny prefix-surviving set we read mi_info_type_id, mi_movie_id, then Y bitset, then varlen mi_info — all cheap because the set is small. This converts 58MB+118MB+626MB strided/random access into 29.5MB sequential access. Expected scan_mi: 24ms -> 3-5ms. To prevent the codegen regression seen in iter_2 and iter_3 (where prefix_dict was prescribed but not actually mmap'd), the storage_extensions.usage and scan_mi_prefix_driven_filter_order sections give the exact code structure. Year threshold 2000 and the four voice-note strings are preserved verbatim.

Iter_2 best at 63ms with scan_mi=24ms (38% of total). Iter_3 (prescribe prefix check inside CSR loop) and iter_4 (sequential scan over all 14.8M mi rows) both regressed because the codegen either did not actually mmap codes.bin or did extra full-table work. Root cause: scan_mi makes 8M random/strided probes into mi_movie_id (58MB), mi_info_off (118MB), and mi_info_dat (626MB) — all greatly exceeding the 12MB L3. The prefix_codes column version already exists; the problem is integrating it correctly. Strategy: Category B (algorithm change) + Category E (use existing storage extension). Make the prefix filter a DEDICATED separate phase build_M_prefix_bitset that sequentially sweeps the 29.5MB codes.bin once (parallel, ~1-2ms) and produces a 1.85MB LLC-resident bitset M_prefix over mi rows. The CSR walk then tests M_prefix[r] as its FIRST inner-loop operation, BEFORE reading mi_movie_id[r], Y, or any varlen mi.info bytes. The ~99.5% of CSR-slice rows that fail the prefix filter incur exactly one cache-line read into the small bitset — no probes into the L3-exceeding columns. Expected: scan_mi drops from 24ms to ~3-6ms; build_M_prefix adds ~1-2ms. Net gain ~17-20ms; total ~43-48ms. Making M_prefix a separate named phase forces codegen to actually mmap codes.bin and use it — distinct from the previously failed inline-check approach. Year threshold 2000 and the four voice-note strings are preserved verbatim.
